newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends well bid, may test higher next week.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends well bid, may test higher next week.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar firmed on Friday and was well supported at the close, dealers said.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.7037/44 and at 67.23 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.7005/10 and 66.90 at the open.
"It's finished the week quite well bid, given the big fall yesterday," said one currency trader.
On Thursday the Reserve Bank said monetary conditions were tighter than necessary, which prompted an immediate rally in the debt market and saw the Kiwi plummet a cent against the U.S. dollar.
But dealers said the currency had bounced strongly off 0.6980 with a change in sentiment.

"I think just a realisation that we're still a high-yielding currency. The global investor is still very yield sensitive and in that respect we're still going to see a lot of offshore demand for the Kiwi," the trader said.
"I think next week we may well have another crack at 71 (US) cents."
Some profit-taking was expected to drag the Kiwi lower in London and New York overnight, but the unit was seen supported at around 0.6920/25.
New Zealand's foreign exchange market will reopen on Tuesday next week after the Labour Day holiday on Monday.
